original_value: Current consumer wearable devices such as smartwatches mostly rely on touchscreen-based user interfaces. Even though touch-based user interfaces help smartphone users quickly adapt to wearable devices with touchscreens, there exist several limitations. In this paper, we propose a non-touchscreen tactile wearable interface as an alternative to touchscreens on wearable devices. We designed and implemented a joystick-integrated smartwatch prototype to demonstrate our non-touchscreen tactile wearable interface. We iteratively improved and updated our prototype to improve and polish interaction ideas and prototype integration. To show feasibility of our approach, we compared and contrasted form factors of our prototype against the latest nine commercial smartwatches in terms of their dimensions. We also show response time and accuracy of our wearable interface to discuss our rationale for an alternative and usable wearable UI. With the proposed tactile wearable user interface, we believe our approach may serve as a cohesive single interaction device to enable various cross-device interaction scenarios and applications.

result.paraphrase: Most current consumer wearables, including smartwatches, depend mainly on touchscreen user interfaces. Although touch-based interfaces help smartphone users adapt quickly to touch-enabled wearables, they still have several drawbacks. In this paper, we present a non-touchscreen tactile wearable interface as an alternative to touchscreen-based wearable devices. To demonstrate this approach, we designed and built a joystick-integrated smartwatch prototype. We refined and updated the prototype through multiple iterations to improve the interaction concepts and the integration of the prototype. To illustrate feasibility, we compared our prototype’s form factor dimensions with those of the latest nine commercial smartwatches. We also report the response time and accuracy of the wearable interface to explain our case for an alternative, usable wearable UI. With the proposed tactile wearable user interface, we believe this approach can act as a unified single interaction device for a variety of cross-device interaction scenarios and applications.
